messages:
Marco (Sales): Heads-up — Cobalt Health (enterprise) is seeing a ~3x p95 latency spike since yesterday's model rollout. They're pushing for a fix or SLA credit.
Tess (Support): Repro steps and logs from their side attached in the ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/COB-342. They say spike ~200ms -> ~650ms on chat completions.
Aisha (PM): Thanks — can eng-runtime confirm if this is the rollout we did (quantized variant v1.3) or something else? Need impact to prioritize.
Ken (Eng-runtime): Looking now. Initial telemetry shows p95 jump roughly aligned with canary flip to quant-v1.3 at 02:14 UTC. CPU on nodes is fine, but GPU kernel fusions show higher tail.
Ken (Eng-runtime): Quick grep of logs shows repeated `kv_cache_miss` for long prefixes for this customer workload. Could be cache invalidation + quant misalignment.
Lina (Eng-platform): We can short-term route Cobalt's traffic to the non-quantized model variant (classic-v1) via route override. It's a config change: `POST /routes/override { "customer": "cobalt", "model": "classic-v1" }`. Low risk.
Aisha (PM): Options: (1) immediate route override (low effort), (2) rollback quant rollout (higher blast radius), (3) deep fix/optimization (longer). Need customer SLA impact and whether they want immediate mitigation vs long-term fix. Marco can we get commitment from Cobalt on routing?
Marco (Sales): I asked them. They want a fast mitigation; will accept route override if it reduces latency while we investigate.
Tess (Support): They reported this is blocking a daytime traffic pattern (APAC), about 17% of their queries.
Aisha (PM): Prioritization criteria for us: (a) percent of customer traffic affected, (b) p95 regression delta, (c) contractual SLA. If (a) >=10% and (b) >=200ms and customer is enterprise, mark P1. Looks like we meet that.
Ken (Eng-runtime): Agreed. I'll prepare a canary rollback plan and perf investigation. For mitigation I'll add a temporary route override and a config to increase batching window to reduce tail: `batching.window_ms = 8 -> 12` (might slightly increase latency for small queries but helps throughput).
Lina (Eng-platform): I can apply route override. Suggest adding an automatic fallback rule: if p95<300ms for 30m, switch back. We have a small script: `./tools/route-toggle --cust cobalt --to classic-v1 --rollback-threshold 300`.
deploy-bot: deploy started by Lina at 2026-03-21T11:34:00Z for route override -> classic-v1 (req #dpl-8842).
deploy-bot: deploy successful on 4/4 nodes (eta ~30s).
Marco (Sales): Cobalt confirmed latency improved in their staging; will test prod in 10m. They asked for ETA for permanent fix.
Aisha (PM): Action items: Ken to own perf root-cause and proposed fix (investigation ticket + rollout plan). Lina to keep route override + watcher in place. Marco to get written acceptance from Cobalt and confirm whether they want rollback to quant later. Product to create backlog ticket with acceptance criteria and launch requirements: regression <50ms p95 vs baseline, end-to-end test covering long-prefix workloads, perf docs + canary gating.
Ken (Eng-runtime): Creating perf ticket now: RD-5817. I'll attach flame graphs and kv-cache traces. ETA for initial RCA: 48h.
Tess (Support): I'll update the customer ticket that we've mitigated with routing and tracking RCA.
Aisha (PM): Thanks team. We'll treat as P1 with mitigation in place and aim for a verified fix in the next sprint. I'll sync with GTM for any SLA comms. :thumbsup:
Marco (Sales): Sending optics to Cobalt now. If they re-confirm production OK, we can close the urgent path and move to roadmap planning for model-variant stability.
Ken (Eng-runtime): Quick note for the backlog item: acceptance criteria should include a non-regression suite with 90th/95th on long-prefix chat prompts and quantized-model kernel microbenchmarks.
Aisha (PM): Agreed — adding those to the ticket. Closing triage in this thread; follow updates in RD-5817 and COB-342.
